## The question

A class measures the resting heart rate of 40 students and wants to say
something about every student at the university. The [[population-mean]]
[[population-mean|symbol]] is unknown. The data give one
[[sample-mean]], [[sample-mean|symbol]] = 68 beats per minute (bpm), with a
sample standard deviation $s = 9$ bpm.

## From one sample to a range

Another class would get a different [[sample-mean]]. The [[se]] measures how
much [[sample-mean|plural]] vary from sample to sample:

$$
\text{SE} = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{9}{\sqrt{40}} \approx 1.42 \text{ bpm}.
$$

A 95% [[ci]] is roughly [[sample-mean|symbol]] ± 2 [[se]], which gives 65.2 to
70.8 bpm.

## What 95% means

The [[confidence-level]] describes the procedure. If many classes repeated the
study and each computed its own interval, about 95% of those
[[ci|short-plural]] would contain [[population-mean|symbol]]. One computed
interval either contains [[population-mean|symbol]] or misses it.

[[sample-mean|cap:plural]] from larger samples vary less, so their
[[ci|short-plural]] are narrower: the [[se|short]] shrinks with $\sqrt{n}$.

::: {.glossary}
:::
